keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for a state Cliopatria lacks: its Liao row starts only in 911 and no Cliopatria shape covers the Khitan lands in 628-906 (Cliopatria's Tang shape reaches only the Chaoyang edge, 7 thousand km2, from 880). The page dates the Dahe Confederation to 'the early 7th century' and its submissions to the Tang to 628 and 648, and places the Khitans 'south of the Xar Moron River' and 'east of the Laoha between Chaoyang'; no area or boundary is given, so a river band and a 100 km disc stand in (confidence 1). The Kumo Xi and Shiwei conquests of Xianzhi (860?-882?) are undated and unplaced, so the shape is not widened.

ledger.note: 628: the Dahe Confederation. 'In the early 7th century, the Dahe clan unified the Khitan tribes in a federation'; 'The Dahe Confederation submitted to the Tang in both 628 and 648'. 628 is the first dated act of the federation (the Neiji tribe under Sun Aocao submitted to the Tang in 619; the Khitans submitted to the Sui in 584). The unification itself is undated, so confidence 2.

ledger.note: 696: the Khitan rebellion. 'In 696, a famine occurred in Khitan territory and [the court] failed to provide relief, sparking a rebellion' (Khitan people page); Li Jinzhong 'rose against the Wu Zhou dynasty in 696 and further invaded Wu Zhou territories' and took the title Wushang Khan; he died on 23 September 696 and Sun Wanrong succeeded him.

730: Dahe supremacy ends. 'The rebellion of Ketuyu ended Dahe supremacy in 730' (Khitan people page: Ketuyu attacked the reigning Khitan ruler in 720, lost to the Tang in 732 and beat a Tang army in 734 with Turkic allies); 'The Yaonian clan had dominated the leadership of the Khitan tribes since the 750s' (Taizu page). Same state, the Yaonian Confederation.

ledger.note: 27 February 907: Abaoji becomes khagan. 'In 907, he appeared at the triennial council and demanded to be named the khagan' with 'the support of seven tribal chiefs' (Taizu page); 'He became khagan of the Khitans on 27 February 907' (the date the liao-dynasty dossier quotes from the same page); 'Abaoji became chieftain of the Yila tribe in 901', 'was named Yuyue' in 903 and 'led 70,000 cavalry into Shanxi' in 905. 'From 907 until 916, Abaoji was beset with constant uprisings and rebellions.'

wars.note: The Li Jinzhong page names no captured prefecture and no 697 events.

wars.name: Ketuyu's rebellion
wars.outcome: Ketuyu attacked the reigning Khitan ruler in 720, ended Dahe supremacy in 730, was defeated by the Tang in 732 and defeated a Tang army in 734 with Turkic allies.

wars.name: An Lushan's Khitan campaigns
wars.outcome: An Lushan 'launched two invasions into Khitan territory in 751 and 755'; the Khitans became vassals of the Uyghurs from 755.

notes:
State Cliopatria lacks: its Liao row starts in 911 and nothing covers the Khitan lands in 628-906; the liao-dynasty dossier already names this slug as predecessor and starts on 27 February 907 on Cliopatria's 911 shape (374 thousand km2, much wider than the homeland).

Dates and places. The pages open date no founding for the Dahe federation ('early 7th century'), none for the Yaonian Confederation, and give no territory except 'south of the Xar Moron River' and 'east of the Laoha between Chaoyang' (both undated, from the New Book of Tang). The shape is therefore a river band plus a disc (confidence 1). Xianzhi's subjugation of the Kumo Xi and Shiwei (860?-882?) and Abaoji's 922 westward step are not placed. The Uyghur overlordship ('the Khitans became vassals of the Uighurs', 755 until 840) and the Tang tributary status of 840-907 are not ledger events here: a vassal_start/vassal_end belongs to the suzerain's dossier (uyghur-khaganate, another group) with this slug as counterpart. The Li Jinzhong page does not mention the prefectures taken in 696-697. The Taizu page says the Yaonian clan led the Khitan tribes 'since the 750s' while the Khitan page gives no date for the Yaonian Confederation's founding; the rename of 730 is dated from the end of Dahe supremacy.

Gaps: Songmo Commandery, Kuge's governorship and Sun Aocao's 619 submission (page undated or pre-628), the 553-605 Northern Qi, Goguryeo and Sui contacts.
